classification.difficultyReason: Apply the named vertical line test to points and curves, checking loops and sideways branches and using open or closed endpoints to decide whether a boundary has multiple outputs.

content.prompt: Decide whether these relations show a function using the vertical line test.

spec.description: Six closed points on numbered Cartesian axes. Between-tick heights are schematic estimates from the source.
spec.mathematics: Distinct inputs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; approximate heights 5, 11, 14, 17, 23, 27. Positive x ticks 1–8; positive y ticks 5–30 in steps of 5.
spec.answerVisibility: Question graph only; supplied answer excluded.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects at most one point.

spec.description: Six closed points; unlabelled heights between ticks are schematic estimates.
spec.mathematics: Distinct inputs 1–6 with approximate heights 11, 5, 14, 11, 5, 17. Positive x ticks 1–7; y ticks 5, 10, 15, 20.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects at most one point. Repeated output values are allowed.

spec.description: Six closed points, including vertically aligned pairs at x=2 and x=4. Between-tick heights are schematic estimates.
spec.mathematics: Approximate plotted positions (1,5), (2,11), (2,23), (3,14), (4,17), (4,27); x ticks 1–8 and y ticks 5–30 by 5.

answer.worked: Not a function: the vertical line $x=2$ intersects two points.

spec.description: Six closed points with a vertically aligned pair at x=2. Between-tick heights are schematic estimates.
spec.mathematics: Approximate plotted positions (1,5), (2,5), (2,14), (4,14), (5,23), (6,17); positive x ticks 1–7 and y ticks 5–25 by 5.

answer.worked: Not a function: the vertical line $x=2$ intersects two points.

spec.description: Unscaled rising straight line with arrows at both ends, negative x-intercept and positive y-intercept.
spec.mathematics: A nonvertical straight line; drawing coordinates specify appearance only and are not printed givens.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the straight line once.

spec.description: Unscaled upward-opening parabola symmetric about the y-axis, vertex below the x-axis and arrows at both upper ends.
spec.mathematics: Single-valued upward parabola with two x-intercepts. Plot parameters are schematic, not supplied numerical givens.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the parabola at most once.

spec.description: Unscaled right-opening parabola with vertex on the negative x-axis and arrows on both branches.
spec.mathematics: Upper and lower branches cross the y-axis. Plot parameters are schematic, not numerical givens.

answer.worked: Not a function: the vertical line through the $y$-axis intersects the curve twice.

spec.description: Unscaled upward V with vertex below the origin, no arrows or markers on its arms.
spec.mathematics: Two straight segments symmetric about the y-axis; each input has at most one output.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the V-shaped graph at most once.

spec.description: Four unlabelled closed points, including two vertically aligned in quadrant I.
spec.mathematics: One point in quadrant II, one in quadrant III, two at the same positive input. Coordinates are schematic and not labelled.

answer.worked: Not a function: a vertical line through the two points in quadrant I intersects both points.

spec.description: Four unlabelled closed points at distinct horizontal positions.
spec.mathematics: One point in quadrant II, one in quadrant III and two in quadrant I; no repeated input. Coordinates are schematic, not labelled.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects at most one point.

spec.description: Increasing cubic-shaped curve through the origin, flattening there, with arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled single-valued S-shaped graph extending into quadrants III and I. Plot coefficient is schematic.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the curve at most once.

spec.description: Circle centred at the origin with four intercept labels, −2 and 2 on each axis.
spec.mathematics: Circle of radius 2: x²+y²=4. Equal coordinate-unit lengths preserve the circular shape.

answer.worked: Not a function: the vertical line $x=0$ intersects the circle at $y=-2$ and $y=2$.

spec.description: Unscaled increasing concave-down curve to the right of the y-axis, crossing the positive x-axis; arrows at both curve ends. Positive axis ends have arrows.
spec.mathematics: Every vertical line meets the curve at most once. The curve has no printed equation or numerical scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph is permanent; supplied classification appears only in the answer.

answer.worked: Every vertical line intersects the graph at most once, so it represents a function.

spec.description: Four-ended Cartesian axes; two upper branches meet at the origin, with a closed teardrop loop below the origin centred on the y-axis.
spec.mathematics: Vertical lines through the loop can intersect the relation more than once.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph is permanent; supplied classification appears only in the answer.

answer.worked: A vertical line through the loop intersects the graph more than once, so it does not represent a function.

spec.description: Curve descends from the upper left to a minimum slightly left of the y-axis, then rises and continuously joins a horizontal rightward ray above the x-axis. Four-ended axes; no numerical scale or endpoint circles.
spec.mathematics: The joined curve and horizontal ray have at most one y-value for each x-value.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph is permanent; supplied classification appears only in the answer.

answer.worked: Every vertical line intersects the graph at most once, including where the curve joins the horizontal ray.

spec.description: Left semicircle centred at the origin, with its upper and lower ends on the y-axis. Four-ended axes; no numerical scale or endpoint circles.
spec.mathematics: Most vertical lines through the semicircle intersect it twice.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph is permanent; supplied classification appears only in the answer.

answer.worked: A vertical line between the leftmost point and the y-axis intersects the semicircle twice, so it does not represent a function.

spec.description: Decreasing curve from the upper left ends at a closed point on the positive x-axis. A horizontal rightward ray starts at an open point directly above that closed point. Four-ended axes; no numerical scale.
spec.mathematics: The two endpoints share an x-coordinate, but only the lower endpoint is included. Every vertical line intersects the relation at most once.
spec.answerVisibility: Endpoint inclusion is permanent; supplied classification appears only in the answer.

answer.worked: Every vertical line intersects the graph at most once. At the shared endpoint x-coordinate, the closed point is included and the open point is excluded, so there is only one output.

spec.description: Three horizontal pieces with shared boundary coordinates and complementary open and closed endpoints; axes have four arrowheads. Coordinates used for drawing are schematic and are not printed numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: Lower leftward ray excludes the y-axis boundary; middle segment includes that boundary and excludes its right boundary; upper rightward ray includes the same right boundary.
spec.answerVisibility: Question diagram contains no supplied classification.

answer.worked: Every vertical line intersects the graph at most once. At each boundary, the open circle is excluded and the closed circle is included, so there is only one output.

spec.description: Two disconnected outward-opening branches with vertices labelled −2 and 2 on the x-axis and four curve arrowheads. Only positive axis ends have arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: Each branch has upper and lower points for x-values beyond its vertex. The schematic curves preserve the source topology; no equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Question diagram contains no supplied classification.

answer.worked: A vertical line through either branch away from its vertex intersects the graph twice, so one input has two outputs.

spec.description: Vertical line at x = 2, arrowheads at both ends, and the printed 2 beside its x-axis intersection. Only positive axis ends have arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: The relation is x = 2.
spec.answerVisibility: Question diagram contains no supplied classification.

answer.worked: The vertical line $x=2$ intersects the graph more than once. The input $2$ has many outputs.

spec.description: Horizontal line at y = −1 with two arrowheads and the printed −1 beside its y-axis intersection. Only positive axis ends have arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: The relation is y = −1.
spec.answerVisibility: Question diagram contains no supplied classification.

answer.worked: Every vertical line intersects the graph exactly once. Each input has the single output $-1$.
